transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-28 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Jordan (Oakbridge Head of Search), Aisha (Oakbridge ML), Tom (Oakbridge Platform)

Summary (auto): quick hands-on demo of embeddings + reranker hosted endpoints, console walkthrough of Optimize suggestions, Q&A on security and pilot next steps.

00:00 Maya: okay everyone, thanks for joining. i'm maya from redwood, i'm the ae on this account. quick round intro?
00:08 Jordan: jordan here, head of search at oakbridge, i'll be driving the backlog for this.
00:12 Aisha: hi i'm aisha, staff ml eng, i'll be running the models and evals.
00:15 Tom: tom, platform eng, i'll own networking / infra stuff.
:19 Samir: samir here, redwood solutions eng, i'll demo the endpoints and run the perf stuff.
00:25 Priya: priya, csm, hi all.
00:28 Maya: cool thanks. quick agenda: embeddings endpoint, then reranker flow (retrieve + rerank), console optimize tips, then security/pilot scoping. we'll leave 10 min for open q's. sound good?
00:37 Jordan: yes sounds good.

01:05 Samir: alright i'm going to share my screen — should see the redwood console and a small notebook. first, embeddings endpoint. backstage, we host a vector endpoint that returns 1536-d vectors for our recommended model, but you can pin smaller models etc.
01:22 Aisha: quick q — what's the default dimension? is it fixed per model or can you request different dims?
01:29 Samir: it's model-specific. the hosted embeddings we show default to 1536 for the medium model; you can select open variants that are 1024 or 768. we compress as needed, and optimize in the console.
01:42 Jordan: and the latency like p95 for embedding calls?
01:46 Samir: on hosted it's typically 30-60ms p95 for single-document embeddings, depends on payload size. we also recommend batching — console suggests batch sizes based on your qps.
01:58 Maya: and cost per embedding call we'll include in the pilot pricing, but batched calls are more cost efficient of course.

03:10 Samir: moving to the retrieval + rerank pipeline — here's an example two-stage flow: first run an ANN search with your vector DB (we integrate with pinecone, weaviate, or you can use in-house), get top-K candidates, then call our hosted reranker endpoint which scores the candidates using a cross-encoder.
03:27 Aisha: is the reranker a separate model family? what about token costs?
03:33 Samir: yes it's separate — reranker is usually a smaller cross-encoder optimized for scoring, it's per-pair scoring so tokenization matters. cost is per-request and per-token on the reranker; we provide batched scoring to amortize overhead. in practice for top-10, you see modest token usage.
03:50 Tom: do you run the reranker on GPUs? what happens under load during end-of-day batch jobs?
03:56 Samir: hosted runs on GPU-backed pools; we autoscale and can bump to dedicated capacity for predictable throughput. for heavy batch jobs we recommend a dedicated or scheduled processing window to avoid latency spikes.

05:40 Samir: ok demo time — notebook: step 1, embed a sample corpus. i call POST /v1/embeddings with three docs, here's the response vectors. note: transcription of sample notebook code in meeting may be fuzzy — code snippet sent as link in chat.
05:58 Jordan: looks straightforward. how do we handle normalization / preproc? tokenization?
06:04 Samir: we show best-practice preproc in the docs. we do recommend stripping headers, normalizing whitespace and preserving short context windows for legal docs.

07:30 Samir: next, I run the ANN in their vector DB — we return top-100, then call our reranker via POST /v1/rerank with query + candidate texts. the reranker returns scores, and we reorder.
07:48 Aisha: during rerank, can we also return structured fields or extraction markers? like passage offsets?
07:54 Samir: yes you can ask the reranker to include offsets or payloads — we return metadata passthrough. caveat: heavy payloads increase latency.

09:20 Jordan: what about caching? if we have repeated queries during trading hours, can we cache embeddings or rerank results?
09:29 Priya: priya here — yes, redwood supports prefix/KV caching for embeddings and model outputs. console has a cache hit rate view and suggestions to tune TTLs.
09:41 Tom: do you store customer data on your side for caching? we need to control retention.
09:46 Priya: caching can be configured for no-persist mode; also you can opt-out of server-side caching. we'll include cache policy options in the security brief.

11:10 Samir: switching to console Optimize — it analyzes your traffic, suggests batch sizes, quantization profiles, and routing rules to hit latency/cost targets. here's a sample suggestion: increase batch to 8 for embeddings to reduce token cost by 22% while keeping p95 under 80ms.
11:33 Aisha: how much of Optimize is automatic vs. manual? can we lock suggestions?
11:38 Samir: it's advisory by default; you can accept a suggestion in the console and it's applied to your dedicated pool if you have one. for hosted we apply safe defaults and show expected impact.

13:05 Jordan: security questions: SOC2 status, KMS, and audit logs — plus we need VPC options for regulated data.
13:13 Maya: we are SOC2 Type II aligned (we'll share the attestation), support KMS for private deployments and host-managed keys for hosted. audit logs are available via the console with export. for VPC, our Private product supports customer VPC and on-prem.
13:33 Tom: if we stay on hosted for pilot, can we have private network peering or dedicated capacity?
13:38 Maya: yes, dedicated pools are an option — reserved capacity can be provisioned per account for predictable latency and isolation. peering options depend on region; we'll confirm.

15:00 Aisha: about data residency — we need EU-only storage for some subsets. do you offer region pinning?
15:06 Priya: yes region pinning is supported for embeddings storage and model serving. we'll capture exact data flows in the security brief.

16:12 Samir: back to performance — i'm going to run a quick live 50-query run against our hosted reranker with a small Oakbridge sample (this is not the full benchmark requested).
16:22 Samir: starting run... [noise] results coming in — avg latency for rerank ~120ms per candidate batch (top 10), p95 ~210ms, note notebook environment and warmup state may affect numbers.
16:45 Jordan: hmm 210ms p95 for rerank — is that with cold start?
16:49 Samir: partially, yes. production with warm caches and dedicated pools will be lower. p95 examples in our benchmarks page show ~150ms for similar configs. we'll run the 1k-query benchmark in a more controlled env for you.

19:10 Aisha: about model explainability — can we get token-level attention or relevance highlights to debug why a doc was scored high?
19:20 Samir: reranker returns score traces and saliency-like signals — it's not full transformer internals, but enough to surface top contributing spans. again heavy debug payloads cost more.

21:05 Tom: networking specifics — we need to know open ports, ip ranges, and whether egress is restricted.
21:12 Priya: we'll attach an operations appendix with recommended firewall rules and IP ranges; for VPC we can route via peering or private link.

23:00 Jordan: pilot success metrics — what does success look like? 10% uplift in click-through relevance? reduce time-to-answer?
23:08 Maya: typical pilots define offline metrics (nDCG, MRR) and online guardrails (CTR, latency SLOs). for Oakbridge maybe target +12% nDCG in held-out eval and p95 latency under 300ms for reranker.
23:25 Jordan: that sounds right. timeline?
23:28 Maya: propose two-week tech integration, then two weeks of benchmark & tuning, then a 4-week pilot in production shadow mode. we can compress if you have support.

25:50 Aisha: are there quotas or rate limits on hosted? we have spikes during end-of-day processing.
25:56 Samir: hosted tiers have soft rate limits but we can provision burst or recommend dedicated capacity for predictable throughput. we can also set up a fallback routing to cheaper model variants if capacity constrained.

28:10 Tom: backup question — if we want to bring the runtime on-prem later, how painful is migration?
28:18 Maya: our Private package is designed for that — same API and config model, so app-level changes are minimal. infra-level ops are heavier but we support the migration with professional services.

30:00 Samir: quick walkthrough of sample rerank payload — POST body includes query, candidate_texts array, and optional metadata. response includes scores, ranking, and you can request detailed spans. code snippets in the repo link.
30:28 Jordan: we'll want language detection — some docs are French.
30:33 Samir: supported — models are multilingual. we recommend using the same model family for embedding + rerank to avoid embedding drift.

32:10 Aisha: pb about tokenization — our legal docs have very long paragraphs. do you chunk?
32:17 Samir: we recommend passage chunking and passing passage-level context to reranker. Optimize can suggest chunk size based on the distribution.

34:40 Priya: circling back to billing — we can create a pilot quote for hosted usage and a reserved capacity option for predictable pricing. Maya will own the quote.

36:15 Maya: note i'll include pilot pricing, an expected cost projection for 3 scenarios (low/med/high qps), and security docs (SOC2, data flow, KMS).

38:50 Jordan: can you show the console view where Optimize suggests batch sizes?
38:55 Samir: yep — sharing console, here's the traffic analyzer, suggestion panel. you can toggle to preview savings and impact on p95.
39:20 Aisha: nice, can you export suggestion history for audits?
39:25 Samir: yes history exports are available as CSV.

41:10 Tom: for the benchmark — what environment will you run it from? will it simulate our network latency?
41:16 Samir: we'll run in our hosted region with a consistent runner. if you want network-internal sim we can run agents from your VPC in a PoC, but that needs a bit more setup.

43:40 Jordan: ok let's recap real quick and confirm next steps.
43:45 Maya: recap: 1) redwood to share pilot quote + security pack; 2) oakbridge to share 10 sample queries and dataset export; 3) redwood to run 1k-query benchmark and return perf table; 4) schedule follow-up to review bench the week of 2026-06-08.
43:59 Jordan: yep, that's what we need.

45:10 Aisha: can you put the expected data retention limits in the security doc? we need 90-day and 1-year options.
45:16 Priya: yes we will include retention policy options and how to purge cache.

47:00 Tom: one more nit: for our change freeze windows (market close), we need no infra updates 17:00-19:00 ET. can you guarantee no scheduled maintenance?
47:09 Maya: for production pilots we'll align maintenance windows and SLA terms, yes.

49:20 Jordan: thanks everyone, i'm optimistic. quick note: we're also evaluating a managed vector db partner but the rerank piece is a differentiator for us.
49:30 Maya: great, we'll include an integration appendix and competitor notes.

51:00 Samir: final quick note — i'll add a sample benchmark script and a link to the notebook used today in the follow-up email.
51:10 Maya: perfect. thanks all. we'll send the follow-up with attachments by next tuesday.
51:20 Jordan: thanks ya.
51:25 Aisha: thanks.
51:30 Tom: bye.

(End of transcript)
